messages:
Maria Chen: heads-up: eu-west1-rack8 node gpu-17 just triggered a fan_stall alert and then the node hit a powercap fallback. Seeing a spike in inference p95 on the fleet.
Jon Patel: oof. any Xid/ECC errors in the logs?
Kai Nguyen: checking logs now, grabbing GPU telemetry.
InfraBot: ALERT: fan_stall detected on node gpu-17 (rack8) at 1956788999. powercap_fallback engaged at 1956789005.
Kai Nguyen: log snippet: `nvmlEvent: FAN_STALL (fan speed=0 rpm)` then `event: power limit exceeded -> powercap fallback to 180W` then a few `Xid 31` kernel warnings around the same time.
Maria Chen: @SRE Oncall can you drain that node? It's servicing low-priority Dedicated pools but still affecting hosted tail latency.
SRE Oncall: on it. Starting graceful drain now, will move pods off gpu-17. Command: `fleetctl drain gpu-17 --grace 300s`
Alex Rivera: telemetry shows others in rack have slightly elevated temps but normal fans. Could be a stuck PWM on that card only. If it's fan hardware, we should replace.
Jon Patel: can we temporarily hard-set a lower powercap to keep latency stable while we drain? e.g., `nvidia-smi -i 17 -pl 150` for the node, then revert after replacement?
Kai Nguyen: We tried soft powercap earlier; default driver ignored it because of firmware policy. But the management controller accepted a lower cap via ipmi for the whole board. Risk: may hit model perf degradation but better than retries.
Maria Chen: tradeoff acceptable. Set it for now and schedule maintenance. Also, create an incident ticket with latency regression tag.
SRE Oncall: set board-level powercap to 160W via IPMI: `ipmitool -H bmc-rack8 -U admin chassis power set 160` (running).
InfraBot: ACTION: node gpu-17 marked DRAINING by SRE Oncall at 1956789050.
Kai Nguyen: after cap applied, p95 dropped from 420ms -> 210ms for the affected routes. Some small increase in token cost but latency acceptable.
Alex Rivera: ordering replacement card (RMA) from vendor. ETA 48h. I'll schedule a hot-swap window.
Jon Patel: note for postmortem: correlate fan PWM telemetry, PMIC logs, and driver Xid 31 timestamps. Might be an intermittent PMIC glitch causing fan to stop then power surge triggers fallback.
Maria Chen: agree. Add model routing fallback to lower-seq-length variants for that rack in case of future similar events.
SRE Oncall: node drained, jobs evac'ed, marking for maintenance. Closing thread after follow-ups are created. :white_check_mark:
